column5: S4: gc converge list reads convergence roots (graph) from rig ledgers; graph beads belong in the city binding. The rig-store convergence writer is the owner of this.
S4: gc converge test-gate reads a convergence root (graph) from the rig ledger by store path.
The test control bead is type=task with only gc.kind=drain, which classifies as work; a production control bead carries graph metadata.

Wisp GC enumerates molecule roots through the graph store only; a work-class (v1 poured) type=molecule root on the work ledger is never reached on a split city. Needs a work leg or a ruling that those are not GC targets.
The test builds beadmail.New over the opened WORK store; production opens mail through openCityMailProvider (messaging class).

S3: order dispatchWisp (order_dispatch.go) pours every order recipe into the graph store without moleculeClassStore; a work-class (v1 poured) recipe lands in the binding, hidden from every work reader.
The test wraps the opened work store as a NudgesStore; production callers pass the nudges class store.

R17: the order gate reads last-run evidence from the orders/graph binding legs only on a split city; a work-class order-run root (v1 poured order formula) on the work ledger is invisible, so cooldown and cursor regress.

The test hands the opened WORK store to resolveSessionIDMaterializingNamed; gc session wake passes the sessions store. Lead to check: cmd_sling.go cliDirectSessionResolver takes the store sling hands it.
Negative input: a work id handed to the session resolver through the sessions store (the right store); not-a-session either way.
